title: NonStationaryBrachistochrone: reproducibility package for controlled-rail brachistochrones in non-stationary spacetimes
description:
Symbolic derivations, numerical verification scripts, figure-generation code, laboratory design studies, and manuscript sources for controlled-rail brachistochrones in non-stationary spacetimes. The repository supports the companion studies of the FLRW and Vaidya sectors and of the conformal Kerr (Thakurta-Kerr) sector.

1.7.2 - every script the manuscripts name, run and checked against what they print. A correction release. It follows a pass that executed each script cited in either paper and compared its output with the number the text quotes, and an independent audit of the proofs.

Two cited checks had no code. ThakurtaMetric/tk_sep_offshell_elliptic.py and VaidyaMetric/vaidya_sep_offshell_elliptic.py contained only a description of the check they were cited for. Both are now executable at thirty digits, each with a control that must fail: the degeneration S = (r - r_d)^2 Q4, the cancellation of the spurious pole at r_d, and the collapse of the letters U_k and W_jk to their elliptic form. The Thakurta-Kerr check now includes the exterior retrograde separatrix r_d = 3.514M, which carries the physical statement and had not been checked before.

Two verification scripts misreported. paper1/verification/verify_section44_closedform.py evaluated the tortoise term of the assembled closed form at the upper limit only, while the printed formula takes it between the limits; the formula agrees with the quadrature to 5e-40, and the script now says so and fails without the bracket. paper1/verification/verify_jacobi_conjugate.wls printed a spurious FAIL for want of the assumption that the scale factor is positive.

Every quoted residual traced to a script. Each number the papers quote without naming a script was traced, re-run and compared. Five had no archived script and now have one: KerrScripts/kerr_tbranch_separatrix_sigma_eval.wls (the t-branch separatrix closed form in Mathematica's Weierstrass functions at forty digits, better than 1e-46 on five arcs, with a control that must fail), kerr_tbranch_genus2_periods.sage.py, kerr_marginal_convergence.py, bvp_missed_roots_highprecision.py and VaidyaMetric/vaidya_tau_spectral_check.py. Where the reproduced value differed from the printed one, the papers now give the reproduced value; two statements with no archived source were withdrawn.

Paper I, proper-time blocks relabelled. The mass of ingoing Vaidya runs with the advanced time, so the drift is weighted by v on every branch. The appendix block that feeds the proper-time density to the block formula is now presented as an algebraic instance, and the v-weighted block as the physical response.

Stated precision brought to what reproduces. The theta-ratio form of the third-kind letter had been quoted at 5e-8; the archived double-precision check gives 7e-5, and the text now rests that identity on Fay's representation of the normalised third-kind differential. separatrix_classification.py applies the selector criterion r_d > 2M stated in the text, not r_d > r_+. A few quoted residuals and one percentage were corrected to the scripts' output, the result-to-script table no longer claims that every entry is generated by the provenance command, and unproven irreducibility statements in Paper I are stated as conjectures, as in Paper II.

Proofs re-read statement by statement. Both manuscripts were re-read against their proofs, first with two local language models and then in an independent audit by GPT-6 Astra, every finding checked by hand and against a computation. Paper I: the branch Hamiltonian is the support function minus the running cost, so free-arrival transversality reads h = 1; the boundary form of the Vaidya first-order source subtracts the elapsed cost clock, the elapsed v on the arrival branch and the elapsed proper time on the proper-time branch, where the earlier text had -lambda on both; the claim that the closed-form extremal is certified up to its first axis crossing is withdrawn, since the caustic comes first and a frozen extremal has a single periapsis; the elliptic letters V_k carry third-kind residues at the points at infinity; the velocity set is an ellipsoid through a projective, not affine, map; the degenerate cases of the reduction system (J = 0, rank 8) are listed; the Hamilton-Jacobi criterion asks for a C1 calibration, competitors that stay in its region and the target condition; the degeneration-family lemma covers the rotating curves. Paper II: the quarter-regime extension of the no-inversion argument and the radius R_* built on it are withdrawn, because the convexity step does not close; a new proposition proves that the proper-time half-angle decreases on explicit regions, for every spin, and is single-peaked for E^2 >= 3/2, so, for frozen A and the symmetric single-periastron family, the fixed-endpoint no-inversion is a theorem wherever the coordinate-time turning point lies in them; the half-angle map is shown not to be single-peaked at low energy, by an interval-certified counterexample; the interval certificates were rerun up to the half-potential radius, at seven static configurations, five of which the proposition now covers analytically; the no-inversion thresholds carry their powers of M; the source numerators are given per branch; the no-conjugate-point proposition assumes E > 1. Both papers: the slow clock of the adiabatic theory is measured from the launch, with the orientation that fixes the signs. A final end-to-end read corrected two general statements and several descriptions: the closed-FLRW example with a = exp(Ht) is no longer called de Sitter (it is not; in de Sitter proper the antipode is out of reach); the claim that a non-Killing selector prevents the optical metric from descending to a quotient is replaced by a direct computation of the optical coefficients for Vaidya and Thakurta-Kerr, since a tuned metric shows the general claim false; the notation for the conformal weight of the angular costate, the scope of the geometric dictionary of the indicatrix, and the description of the tau-separatrix figure were made precise. Several verification scripts no longer print conclusions the manuscripts have withdrawn, and vacuous checks were replaced by notes or by real tests. Paper II now states its relation to brachistochrone-ruled timelike surfaces (its separation equation is the Jacobi equation of their rulings in conformal Kerr at frozen A), to totally geodesic 2-planes of weighted solitons, and to curvature-operator methods (the spectrum of the frozen Schwarzschild optical curvature operator enters the Jacobi equations), and cites the soliton literature it draws on.

What did not change. No closed form or figure changes, and every verification script exits cleanly. The provenance check regenerates the manifest and the adiabatic slopes identically. Thirty-two manifest entries; content digest 42ed5ab1779c5813.
